ETCS-i Control
Through centralized control by the engine control computer, engine output relative to the accelerator opening is optimally controlled, achieving good accelerator controllability and vehicle stability over the entire driving range.
The functions of normal throttle opening control (non-linear control), idle speed control (ISC), traction control (including VSC) and cruise control have been integrated into the 1-valve type electronically controlled throttle body.
Through integrated control with the powertrain system, excellent handling stability and comfort are achieved, ensuring vehicle stability.
To allow driving in the unlikely event of a malfunction, the system has a 2-system redundant configuration to ensure reliability.
ETCS-i Control List
Throttle Valve Control Normal Control Controls the throttle valve opening to generate engine output according to the driving conditions and accelerator pedal opening.
Radar Cruise Control Enables constant speed driving, including vehicle-to-vehicle distance control, based on the signal from the distance control computer.
ECT + EFI + ETCS-i Integrated Control (Shift Shock Reduction Control) Controls the throttle valve opening during ECT shifting to reduce shift shock during upshifts and downshifts and shorten shift time.
Maximum Speed Control When the vehicle speed reaches 180km/h, the throttle valve is closed to restrict any increase in vehicle speed.
TRC (VSC) + ETCS-i Cooperative Control Stabilizes the vehicle through communication with the skid control computer when TRC and VSC are operating.
Idle Speed Control (ISC) Controls the fast idle speed according to the engine coolant temperature and the idle speed after engine warm-up. In addition, the idle speed is controlled through the fuel injection volume and throttle opening.

Accelerator Position Sensor Detects the accelerator opening.
Intake and Exhaust Cam Position Sensors Detects the actual camshaft angle.
Crankshaft Position Sensor Detects the crank angle (engine speed).
Water Temperature Sensor Detects the engine coolant temperature.
Starter Relay Sends the starter voltage during engine starting as the starter signal.
Neutral Start Switch Detects the P, N and D positions of the A/T.
Combination Meter Receives the vehicle speed signal (SP1) and sends the vehicle speed signal (SPD).
